rot.ideia.ex1.e1: Now the pieces will meet. The white rook is on d1; a black knight is on d6.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: The rook reaches d6: the file is clear up to there. When a piece reaches an enemy piece, we say it attacks it.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: Capturing means moving to the square of an enemy piece. The captured piece leaves the board.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Capture the knight with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! The knight left the board, and the rook took its place.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes up the d-file and captures the knight on d6.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: The rook went to an empty square. Let's go back: the knight is on d6.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Capture the knight with the rook, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: Each piece captures the way it moves: the rook in a straight line, the bishop diagonally, the knight in an L.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Only the pawn is different: it moves straight but captures diagonally, as you have seen.
rot.ideia.ex1.l3: Remember the idea: capturing means taking the enemy piece's square.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: The queen reaches two black knights: one on a4 and another on d5.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: A piece protects another of its side when it reaches that square. The pawn on e6 protects the knight on d5.
rot.ideia.ex2.e3: Whoever captures a protected piece is captured back. The knight on a4 is loose: nobody protects it.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Capture the knight that is loose, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! A knight up, and the queen is still safe.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The queen captures the loose knight on a4.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.1: The queen captures the knight on d5...
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.2: ...but the pawn captures the queen back. You traded your queen for a knight.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1d5.3: Let's go back and look for the loose piece.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: The queen went to an empty square. Let's go back: capture one of the knights.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Capture the knight that is loose, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: Before capturing, look at each enemy piece and see, by the way it moves, whether it reaches that square.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: Remember the idea: a loose piece can be captured without fear; a protected one, only if the trade pays off.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Now I will show the value of each piece and when a trade pays off.
rot.demos.valores.e1: To decide on a trade, count the value of the pieces.
rot.demos.valores.l1: The pawn is worth 1. The knight and the bishop are worth 3 each.
rot.demos.valores.l2: The rook is worth 5, and the queen, the strongest piece, is worth 9.
rot.demos.valores.l3: The king has no trade value: he never leaves the board. Attacking the king is called check, the next lesson.
rot.demos.trocaBoa.e1: The knight on d5 is protected by the pawn on e6. Even so, the white pawn can capture it.
rot.demos.trocaBoa.l3: White gave a pawn, worth 1, and won a knight, worth 3. Giving the cheaper piece for the dearer one is a good trade.
rot.demos.proteger.e1: The black rook attacks the knight on d4: it is loose.
rot.demos.proteger.l1: The pawn steps up to e3. Since it captures diagonally forward, it now protects d4.
rot.demos.proteger.l2: If the rook captures the knight...
rot.demos.proteger.l3: ...the pawn captures the rook: it is worth 5, and the knight 3.
rot.demos.proteger.l4: An attacked, loose piece is in danger: protect it, as here, or take it to a square nobody attacks.
rot.demos.proteger.l5: Now it's your turn: in the next positions, capture the loose piece and protect your own.
rot.pratica.pecaSolta.enunciado: The bishop reaches two black pieces. Capture the loose one, in one move.
rot.pratica.pecaSolta.fim: Perfect. The rook was loose: you won 5 without losing anything.
rot.pratica.pecaSolta.err.f1d3: The pawn on c4 protects the knight: it would capture your bishop. Try again.
rot.pratica.protegerBispo.enunciado: The black rook attacks your bishop on c4. Protect it with a pawn, in one move; there are two ways.
rot.pratica.protegerBispo.fim: Well done. Now you know how to capture, protect and count the value of the pieces.
rot.pratica.protegerBispo.err.b2b4: From there the pawn does not reach c4. It must stand one square below the bishop, diagonally.
rot.pratica.protegerBispo.err.d2d4: From there the pawn does not reach c4. It must stand one square below the bishop, diagonally.
